output.summary: A gymnosperm native to southern Japan, including the Ryukyu Islands, it has a thick, fibrous trunk crowned with glossy dark-green leaves. Its pith supplies edible starch for sago only after careful repeated washing and cooking to remove toxins; seeds should not be eaten, and all parts are toxic.
output.edibilityNote: Pith starch is made into sago after careful repeated washing and cooking; seeds should not be eaten, and all plant parts contain toxins.
